title: Finite-support components and inverses for double evaluation
statement:
Let $R$ be a commutative ring, and let $P,J,I$ be cochain complexes of $R$-modules [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Suppose every $P^s$ is finite free (has a finite basis [def-weil-pbc-free-module]), and fix integers $u,\ell,a,b$ with $a\le b$, $P^s=0$ for $s>u$, $J^j=0$ for $j<\ell$, and $I^p=0$ for $p\notin[a,b]$. No injectivity assumption on $I$ or $J$ is imposed. Use the product total Hom of [def-sc-module-total-hom-complex] and direct-sum tensor totalization of [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves], specialized to ordinary modules, with the module tensor product of [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. Put $H=\operatorname{Hom}_R^\bullet(J,I)$, $A=\operatorname{Hom}_R^\bullet(P,J)$, $T=\operatorname{Tot}(H\otimes_R P)$ and $B=\operatorname{Hom}_R^\bullet(A,I)$. For every integer $n$, let $S_n=\{(p,r,s)\in\mathbf Z^3:p+r+s=n,\ a\le p\le b,\ r\le-\ell,\ s\le u\}$. Then $S_n$ is finite, with $n-b+\ell\le s\le u$ and $n-b-u\le r\le-\ell$. The product defining $A^k$ has only $\ell-k\le s\le u$ potentially nonzero factors. The canonical component projections and inclusions give module isomorphisms
$$T^n\cong\bigoplus_{(p,r,s)\in S_n}\operatorname{Hom}_R(J^{-r},I^p)\otimes_R P^s,\qquad B^n\cong\bigoplus_{(p,r,s)\in S_n}\operatorname{Hom}_R(\operatorname{Hom}_R(P^s,J^{-r}),I^p).$$
Under these identifications the degree-$n$ signed evaluation map is an isomorphism: its $(p,r,s)$ component is
$$g\otimes x\longmapsto\bigl(f\longmapsto(-1)^{s(r+1)}g(f(x))\bigr).$$
For a finite basis $(e_i)$ of $P^s$, define $\iota_i:J^{-r}\to\operatorname{Hom}_R(P^s,J^{-r})$ by $\iota_i(v)(e_j)=\delta_{ij}v$. The inverse component sends $\beta$ to $(-1)^{s(r+1)}\sum_i(\beta\circ\iota_i)\otimes e_i$. This asserts invertibility of the specified maps of modules; it makes no assertion about compatibility with differentials or derived morphisms.

source.place: Tag 0A68, lemma-internal-hom-evaluate-isomorphism, proof of case (2): finite-support ranges and maps c_{p,r,s}; finite-free specialization with explicit component inverse

proof.text: Fix $n$. For $(p,r,s)\in S_n$, $s=n-p-r\ge n-b+\ell$ and $r=n-p-s\ge n-b-u$. Hence $S_n$ is a subset of the finite integer box $[a,b]\times[n-b-u,-\ell]\times[n-b+\ell,u]$. An empty interval gives the empty set; thus this argument also covers degrees with no potentially nonzero term.

source.place: Tag 0A68, lemma-internal-hom-evaluate-isomorphism, proof of case (2): finite-support ranges and maps c_{p,r,s}; finite-free specialization with explicit component inverse

proof.text: By the total Hom definition, $A^k=\prod_s\operatorname{Hom}_R(P^s,J^{s+k})$. A factor is zero if $s>u$ or $s+k<\ell$. Projection onto $\ell-k\le s\le u$ and extension by zero are mutually inverse linear maps: each omitted coordinate belongs to a zero module. Thus $A^k$ is the finite product over that interval. For any finite family $(M_i)$ the product identifies with its direct sum: $(m_i)\mapsto\sum_i\mathrm{in}_i(m_i)$ and $\sum_i\mathrm{in}_i(m_i)\mapsto(m_i)$ are inverse, coordinate by coordinate.

source.place: Tag 0A68, lemma-internal-hom-evaluate-isomorphism, proof of case (2): finite-support ranges and maps c_{p,r,s}; finite-free specialization with explicit component inverse

proof.text: Write $h=n-s$. The total Hom definition gives $H^h=\prod_{p+r=h}\operatorname{Hom}_R(J^{-r},I^p)$. Projection and zero extension restrict this product to $a\le p\le b$, $r\le-\ell$; this is finite since $r=h-p$. Apply the cited finite-product tensor isomorphism with $N=P^s$ and these Hom modules (including the empty family). It sends $g\otimes x$ to $(g_{p,r}\otimes x)_{p,r}$. The tensor totalization has $T^n=\bigoplus_{h+s=n}H^h\otimes_RP^s$. Its nonzero summands require $s\le u$ and $n-s=h\le b-\ell$, hence $s\ge n-b+\ell$. Reindex the resulting finite pairs by $(p,r,s)\in S_n$ and identify finite products with sums by step 2. This gives exactly the asserted isomorphism for $T^n$; all maps are the specified component maps.

source.place: Tag 0A68, lemma-internal-hom-evaluate-isomorphism, proof of case (2): finite-support ranges and maps c_{p,r,s}; finite-free specialization with explicit component inverse

proof.text: The total Hom definition gives $B^n=\prod_p\operatorname{Hom}_R(A^{p-n},I^p)$, with only $a\le p\le b$ contributing. In step 2 take $k=p-n$. Denote the projection and zero-coordinate inclusion for its finite factors by $\pi_s$ and $j_s$. A linear map $\beta:A^k\to I^p$ corresponds to $(\beta\circ j_s)_s$, with inverse $(\beta_s)_s\mapsto\sum_s\beta_s\circ\pi_s$, since $\sum_sj_s\pi_s=1$ and $\pi_sj_t=\delta_{st}$. Set $r=n-p-s$. The condition $\ell-k\le s\le u$ is precisely $r\le-\ell$, $s\le u$, and $s+k=-r$. This reindexes the finite family as $S_n$ and yields the stated isomorphism for $B^n$. No interchange of Hom with an infinite product is used.

source.place: Tag 0A68, lemma-internal-hom-evaluate-isomorphism, proof of case (2): finite-support ranges and maps c_{p,r,s}; finite-free specialization with explicit component inverse

proof.text: Fix a triple in $S_n$ and abbreviate $V=P^s$, $W=J^{-r}$, $U=I^p$, and $\epsilon=(-1)^{s(r+1)}$. The assignment $(g,x)\mapsto(f\mapsto\epsilon g(f(x)))$ is $R$-bilinear in $(g,x)$, and its value is an $R$-linear map in $f$, by linearity of evaluation and commutativity of $R$. The tensor universal property therefore defines a linear map $C:\operatorname{Hom}_R(W,U)\otimes_R V\to\operatorname{Hom}_R(\operatorname{Hom}_R(V,W),U)$ with the asserted formula on pure tensors.

source.place: Tag 0A68, lemma-internal-hom-evaluate-isomorphism, proof of case (2): finite-support ranges and maps c_{p,r,s}; finite-free specialization with explicit component inverse

proof.text: Choose a finite basis $(e_i)$ of $V$, and write $\lambda_i:V\to R$ for its coordinate linear maps, so $x=\sum_i\lambda_i(x)e_i$. Define $\iota_i(v)(x)=\lambda_i(x)v$; this is linear in $v$ and $x$, and on $e_j$ it is $\delta_{ij}v$. Consequently $D(\beta)=\epsilon\sum_i(\beta\circ\iota_i)\otimes e_i$ is a well-defined linear map in $\beta$, with the stated inverse formula.

source.place: Tag 0A68, lemma-internal-hom-evaluate-isomorphism, proof of case (2): finite-support ranges and maps c_{p,r,s}; finite-free specialization with explicit component inverse

proof.text: For every $f:V\to W$, the basis expansion gives $f=\sum_i\iota_i(f(e_i))$: evaluating at $x$ gives $\sum_i\lambda_i(x)f(e_i)=f(x)$. Hence $C(D(\beta))(f)=\epsilon^2\sum_i\beta(\iota_i(f(e_i)))=\beta(f)$, since $\epsilon^2=1$ and $\beta$ is linear. This proves $CD=1$, including an empty basis.

source.place: Tag 0A68, lemma-internal-hom-evaluate-isomorphism, proof of case (2): finite-support ranges and maps c_{p,r,s}; finite-free specialization with explicit component inverse

proof.text: It remains to check $DC=1$ on pure tensors, which generate the tensor product. For $g:W\to U$ and $x\in V$, one has $(C(g\otimes x)\circ\iota_i)(v)=\epsilon\lambda_i(x)g(v)$. Therefore $D(C(g\otimes x))=\epsilon^2\sum_i(\lambda_i(x)g)\otimes e_i=\sum_i g\otimes\lambda_i(x)e_i=g\otimes x$, using the balancing relation and the basis expansion. Linearity gives $DC=1$ everywhere.

source.place: Tag 0A68, lemma-internal-hom-evaluate-isomorphism, proof of case (2): finite-support ranges and maps c_{p,r,s}; finite-free specialization with explicit component inverse

proof.text: Take the direct sum of the component maps $C$ and their inverses $D$ over the finite set $S_n$, and compose with the two identifications from steps 3 and 4. The two compositions are the identity on each coordinate, hence on the whole direct sum. This is the specified signed degree-$n$ evaluation isomorphism with the specified inverse. If $S_n$ is empty both sides are zero. Since $n$ was arbitrary, every asserted degree is covered; neither injectivity nor any calculation with differentials was needed.
